analysis:
The PR threads a new `minimumGrantBytes` parameter into `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` at every call site in StandaloneServer.swift: the reserve preflight (~1040), the load-time reslice (~1207-1237), `resliceGrowSurvivors` (~1389), and the native MiMo load path in StandaloneServer+NativeMiMo.swift (~375). It also adds a helper, `Self.minimumGrantBytes(_:)`, which builds the per-model floor dictionary from `existing.map { ($0.slot.modelId, $0.minimumGrantBytes) }`. This is a memory-sizing/availability change. The goal is to stop a load or regrow from shrinking a slot below its serviceability floor. It does not touch the plaintext prompt path, encryption, attestation, authorization, or the cache storage and crypto code covered by T-041.

The `resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable` refusal check is retained, so the fail-loud floor still applies.

One point I could not verify: `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` traps on duplicate keys. Slot model IDs should be unique per `slots`, and `existingSlotGrants(excludingModelId:)` is not shown. If a duplicate ever arose, the result would be a process crash (availability), not a data leak. The pre-existing code already used the same construction, so this is not new.

The new `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` signature and its semantics for `minimumGrantBytes` are outside the supplied evidence. Unclear semantics there could affect the budget invariant Σ(grants) ≤ fleet budget, an availability and memory-safety matter relevant to T-029-style resource concerns.

The NativeMiMo retirement code is shown as unchanged context; only the one reslice call was modified. I did not examine unchanged callers.

No security regression is identified. A residual question for integration is whether `resliceGrants` with floors can exceed the fleet KV budget when floors sum above the budget. Verify that the post-call serviceability check or budget enforcement still bounds this.
